full_judgment:
M Moazzam Husain J : This Rule is directed against the order dated 15-11-2003 passed by the learned District Judge, Tangail, in Miscellaneous Case No. 51 of 2003 refusing to withdraw the Miscellaneous Case No. 64 of 1998 (correspondent to Misc. Case No. 39 of 1993) to his own Court from the Court of the Special District Judge, Tangail. 

 2. Facts relevant for disposal of this rule, in short, are that the present petitioner borrowed an amount of money from the House Building Finance Corporation, shortly, "HBFC" but, according to HBFC, he fell into arrear of payment leaving as of 31-8-1993 a total amount of Taka 15 lakh and odd overdue on the loan account. HBFC filed Miscellaneous Case No. 39 of 1993 under Article 27 of the Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation Order, 1973, (P0 No. VII of 1973) in the Artha Rin Adalat, Tangail, for realization of the loan-money. 

 3. Subsequently the HBFC, however, moved an application before the District Judge, Tangail, praying for transferring the Miscellaneous Case from the Artha Rin Adalat to the Court the District Judge in view of Article 27 of PO No. VII of 1973. The Miscellaneous Case No. 39 of 1993 was accordingly transferred to the Court of the District Judge from the Artha Rin Adalat and was renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 68 of 1998 as aforesaid. The present petitioner as opposite party in the Miscellaneous Case was accordingly served with notice of the transfer and tendency of the case in the Court of the District Judge, Tangail. He also made appearance in the Miscellaneous Case and filed written objection denying in material particulars all the allegations made therein against him. 

 4. During tendency of the Miscellaneous Case in the Court of the District Judge as above the learned District Judge, all on a sudden transferred the same to the Court of the Special District Judge, Tangail, by his order dated 27-9-2003 allegedly without allowing the petitioners an opportunity to be heard. The petitioner having come to know about the transfer moved an application under Sections 24 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the District Judge, for withdrawing the case to his own Court from the Court of the Special District Judge for disposal on the grounds, inter alia, that under Article 27 of PO No. VII of 1973, it is the exclusive jurisdiction of the 'District Judge' to try and dispose of such cases. The Special District Judge is not competent to entertain the Case for hearing and disposal. 

 6. Mr Abul Quasem, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner took us through the provisions of Article 27 of PO No. VII of 1973 and submitted that the Order is a special law providing special procedure for speedier realization of loan from the defaulting borrower through specified forum, i.e. the Court of the 'District Judge' having territorial jurisdiction over the concerned property of the borrower. No other Court, therefore, has jurisdiction to entertain the application to be made by the HBFC as contemplated by law. Learned Advocate further submits that the Miscellaneous Case was transferred to the Court of the District Judge from the Artha Rin Adalat by reference to the case of Jahan Ara Akhter Begum a HBFC reported in 47 DLR 158. The error, he submitted, corrected earlier was subsequently committed by the learned District Judge on wrong proposition of law. The impugned order, according to him, is ex facie illegal in that it has sought to confer jurisdiction on a Court which has no jurisdiction conferred by law. 

 7. No one appears on behalf of the opposite parties. It is apparent on records that an application (Annex-A) under Article 27 of the PO No. VII of 1973, was initially filed by the HBFC in the Artha Rin Adalat, Tangail, amongst others, for permission to sell the property of the petitioner mortgaged to the Corporation as security against loan taken by him. The application gave rise to Miscellaneous Case bearing No. 39 of 1993. It is also clear that at one stage the Miscellaneous Case was transferred to the Court of the District Judge, wherein it was renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 68 of 1998. The present petitioner appeared in Miscellaneous Case No. 68 of 1998 and filed written objection against the claim set out in the application by HBFC made against him. It is not clear how and for what reasons the Miscellaneous Case was subsequently transferred to the Court of the Special District Judge, Tangail. But the impugned order read with the application for withdrawal (Annex-C) filed by this petitioner suggests that the Miscellaneous Case was transferred by the District Judge to the former Court by his order dated 27-9-2003 for disposal and the same is now pending as such for disposal. 

 8. The case involves a clear question of law touching upon the jurisdiction of the Court now in seisin of the matter. 

 9. In the case of Jahan Ara Akhter begum, referred to above, several applications of similar nature filed by the HBFC were pending before the District Judge, Tangail. Meanwhile Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 came into being. In view of the new promulgated for realization of loan granted by the financial institutions those applications were transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat at the instance of HBFC. The borrower opposite-parties filed application before the District Judge, Tangail, to withdraw the applications to his own Court from the Artha Rin Adalat in view of Article 27 of the PO No. VII of 1973. The Miscellaneous Case that arose out of the application was dismissed by the District Judge which was challenged before the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division held: 

 we are of the view that the cases for realization of loan of the HBFC shall be instituted in the Court of the learned District Judge and the same would be heard and disposed of by the District Judge, according to the provisions of Article 27 of the PO No. VII of 1973. " 

 10. The case does not appear to be exactly on point in that the same was decided essentially on the question of jurisdictional controversy between the District judge and the Artha Rin Adalat emanating from two separate legislations. Here in this case law is the same but the District Judge transferred the Miscellaneous Case to another Judge called 'Special District Judge'; according to him, of co-equal Jurisdiction under the same law. The instant case, therefore, involves an intricate question of jurisdiction of two Courts claiming co-equal jurisdiction under the same law rather than the question of application of law to two Courts created under two different enactments. The decision, thus, is hardly of any avail for our purpose. 

 15. Even if the motive of the party is bad, when a question of law as important as one relatable to the question of jurisdiction is raised there is no scope for sidestepping the same. Since a decision of the superior Court as well as particular provisions of law were referred to i him it was his obligation to go through and give his opinion about their applicability or otherwise in the case. This is a kind of judicial act which cannot but be strongly disapproved. 

 16. We, for ourselves, do not find any reason to give any extended meaning to the plain and unambiguous expression "District Judge" consistently used in the law itself and import any other designation of Judges therein irrespective of their co-equal jurisdiction, if any. Even it is the case that the Special District Judge is the District Judge himself still the application is to be hard by him in his capacity as the District Judge not as Special District Judge. 

 17. For all the reasons stated above we find merit in the rule. In the result the rule is made absolute. The impugned orders dated 15-11-2003 and 27-9-2003 passed by the learned District Judge, Tangail, are set aside. The Miscellaneous Case No. 68 of 1998 now pending in the Court of the Special District Judge, Tangail, is transferred to the Court of the District Judge, Tangail, for hearing and disposal. The order of say passed earlier is herby vacated.
